abstract: Between 1990 and 2000, 56 consecutive patients underwent lung resection for removal of metastatic disease. Mortality, disease-free interval, and overall survival were studied. Only patients with a complete follow-up were included and data were collected conform the protocol of the International Registry of Lung Metastases. The primary tumour in our series was an epithelial tumour in 25 patients (45%), sarcoma in 15 (27%), germ cell tumours in 11 (19%) and melanoma in 5. Operative mortality was 1.4% (1 out of 73 procedures). Germ cell tumours had the best survival (76% at 5 years), and melanoma the worst (0% at 5 years). Multivariate analysis showed that survival for patients who underwent 2 or more metastasectomies was surprisingly good with a 5-year survival rate of 46%. Survival was not related to disease-free interval, multiple lung metastases, or pneumonectomy. It is in accordance with some reports that a short disease-free interval, numerous lung metastases, or recurrence after the first metastasectomy should not preclude patients from operation.
abstract_ja: 1990年から2000年の間に、肺転移の外科的切除を受けた連続56例を対象とした。対象の転移性疾患は、国際肺転移登録のプロトコルに従ってデータ収集された。原発腫瘍は上皮性腫瘍25例(45%)、肉腫15例(27%)、胚細胞腫瘍11例(19%)、黒色腫5例であった。手術死亡率は1.4%(73手術中1例)であった。胚細胞腫瘍は5年生存率76%と最も良好で、黒色腫は0%と最も不良であった。多変量解析では、2回以上の転移切除を受けた患者の5年全生存率は46%と予想外に良好であった。生存は無病期間、肺転移の個数、肺全摘術とは関連しなかった。無病期間の短さ、多数の肺転移、初回転移切除後の再発があっても手術の適応を妨げるべきではないという報告とも一致する。
